name: TallyPrime
real_strength: A desktop accounts package many Indian accountants already know. The buy page sells a single-PC Silver licence and a multi-PC Gold licence, including rental terms.
price_as_listed: Silver lifetime ₹22500 plus 18% GST. Gold lifetime ₹67500 plus 18% GST. Silver one-month rental ₹750 plus 18% GST. Gold one-month rental ₹2250 plus 18% GST. TSS renewal amount is not copied: the buy page says some plans include TSS and does not state a separate TSS rupee amount in the same plain sentence as the licence price.
gst_treatment: excluding GST; the page adds 18% GST
when_they_are_the_better_buy: The firm wants to stay on the desktop package the accountant already runs, on one or a few PCs.
when_we_are_the_wrong_choice: We are the wrong choice when the firm wants that desktop file to be read in automatically. We have no Tally company reader.

name: Zoho Books
real_strength: Cloud accounting with a free plan for a small firm, and paid plans that add users, inventory on the Professional plan, and warehouses plus serial numbers on the Elite plan.
price_as_listed: Free plan while financial-year revenue does not exceed 25 lakhs. Standard ₹749, Professional ₹1499, Premium ₹2999 per organisation per month, billed annually. Elite ₹4999 per organisation per month. Ultimate has no rupee figure in the retrieved text.
gst_treatment: GST treatment not stated on the page
when_they_are_the_better_buy: The firm wants a packaged cloud subscription it can start without an implementation project, and it fits the plan limits on the page.
when_we_are_the_wrong_choice: We are the wrong choice when a subscription on that page covers the job and the firm does not want a scoped implementation.

name: Zoho Inventory
real_strength: The India pricing URL returned dollar prices and a note that the offer applies to new customers in the US region. Listed strengths on that response include locations, batches, and serials on higher plans. Those dollars are not recorded as an India price.
price_as_listed: India rupee price not stated on the page retrieved.
gst_treatment: not applicable; no INR price recorded
when_they_are_the_better_buy: The firm wants a packaged inventory subscription and is buying in the region that page prices.
when_we_are_the_wrong_choice: We are the wrong choice when that packaged inventory plan is enough and the firm does not want implementation.

name: Busy
real_strength: Desktop and subscription accounting with godowns, GST e-returns, and a stated path for e-invoice and e-way on the paid GST plans. Express is free.
price_as_listed: BUSY 21 Basic ₹11000, Standard ₹16500, Enterprise ₹22000. BUSY Magic Start ₹5000, Smart ₹8000, Power ₹12000, Power+ ₹50000, each per 360 days. The page's cost example says prices exclude GST.
when_they_are_the_better_buy: The firm wants a known Indian desktop or subscription package and the GST features that page lists.
when_we_are_the_wrong_choice: We are the wrong choice when that package already does the job and the firm does not want a separate implementation.

name: Marg ERP
real_strength: A published India price list for Nano, Basic, Silver, and Gold, with extra-user prices and GST called out on the page.
price_as_listed: Nano ₹5550, Basic ₹10300, Silver ₹13900, Gold ₹26000. The page says 18% GST extra.
gst_treatment: excluding GST; the page says 18% GST extra
when_they_are_the_better_buy: The firm wants that published licence and will buy it from the vendor, not from an online portal the vendor says it does not support.
when_we_are_the_wrong_choice: We are the wrong choice when that licence covers the firm and they do not want a scoped move onto another system.

name: Vyapar
real_strength: A low monthly billing and stock tool. The page shows invoicing, stock, and GST reports for a small business.
price_as_listed: The page shows ₹242 per month. A struck figure of ₹350 is also on the page. The asterisk is not explained in the retrieved text.
gst_treatment: GST treatment not stated on the page
when_they_are_the_better_buy: A smaller counter wants a cheap billing app and the monthly price on that page.
when_we_are_the_wrong_choice: We are the wrong choice for a firm that is still that size and does not need an implementation.

name: SAP Business One
real_strength: The vendor page describes one system for accounting, purchasing, inventory, sales, and reporting, with cloud or on-premise deployment. The page does not list a public price.
price_as_listed: Price not stated on the page.
gst_treatment: GST treatment not stated because no price is stated
when_they_are_the_better_buy: The firm has chosen that vendor and a partner-led project, and it will take the sales process on that page.
when_we_are_the_wrong_choice: We are the wrong choice when the firm wants that vendor's name and a partner project rather than this scoped offer.

name: Odoo
real_strength: The pricing page sells a per-user subscription that includes the apps in the plan, and it says implementation service is not included.
price_as_listed: One App Free at $0. Standard US$31.10 per user per month. Custom US$61.00 per user per month. The page says the discount is valid for 12 months for the initial users ordered.
gst_treatment: GST treatment not stated on the page
when_they_are_the_better_buy: The firm wants that per-user subscription and will hire implementation separately, which the page says is not included.
when_we_are_the_wrong_choice: We are the wrong choice when the firm has already chosen that subscription and a different implementer.

name: Local custom vendor
real_strength: A category, not a firm. A local shop can build exactly what the owner describes and sit in the same city. No firm is named, because naming one would invent a competitor we did not fetch.
price_as_listed: Price not stated. There is no public page for an unnamed shop.
when_they_are_the_better_buy: The firm wants custom software shaped around one site, and it accepts a single vendor who wrote that code.
when_we_are_the_wrong_choice: We are the wrong choice when the firm wants bespoke software rather than a scoped setup of the system we already have.
